screenings.title: Dust in the Wind
screenings.description: Young lovers Wan and Huen, fresh out of junior high school in the remote, mountainous mining town where they were raised, look forward to a bright future together in their new home of Taipei—only to face first the grim reality of urban life there, then a three-year separation, after Wan is drafted into the Republic of China Army, which ultimately proves fatal to their affections. Based on the personal experiences of frequent Hou co-screenwriter Wu Nien-jen, the poignant, plangent Dust in the Wind has emerged as a popular favorite among Hou’s films, his first collaboration with composer Chen Ming-chang and actor Li Tian-lu, which also features some of Mark Lee Ping-bing’s most hypnotically beautiful tracking shots.

screenings.title: Junk Dump Film Festival 2026: Day Two
screenings.description: Museum of the Moving Image and Junk Dump Magazine will present Junk Dump’s sixth annual short film festival. Junk Dump Magazine is a not-for-profit arts organization that produces a semi-annual print publication and events like Junk Dump Film Festival, which highlights emerging and underrepresented filmmakers working at the intersection of video art and storytelling. The festival presents a curated program of narrative, animated, and experimental short films made by artists using unique processes to tell singular and engaging stories. This year’s selection was guest judged and curated by two New York–based filmmakers. Caroline Mariko Stucky (she/they) is an award-winning Swiss-Japanese cinematographer, and the founder and creative director of CM8 Productions, a film and video production company specializing in independent films, music videos, and fashion films. Sidney Rose White is a Texas-born actress, model, and illustrator based in New York City. She can be seen in Wes and Kyra, HULU’s Red Is the Color of Beauty, Awesome, and Schon! Magazine’s Sheltering with You. Day Two programming will include a selection of nine experimental and animated shorts. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers. Screening run time approx. 80 mins. Featuring: Through the Fog Dir. William Bishop. 2026, 8 mins. U.S. Littlefish Dir. Yuhyeon Byun. 2025, 9 mins. Czechia/U.S. A young woman relies on a magical rybička with the ability to answer any question to navigate her unresolved feelings for a man she once shared an intense connection with. The Frame Dir. Caroline Johnson. 2025, 3 mins. U.S. How do you depict the undepictable? The frame: a container. a boundary. a moment. Is it a unit of time or space—or of both? The existence of a frame necessarily implies something within, and consequently something outside. The Frame is an exploration of spatial and temporal boundaries through the lens of paintings of the late Renaissance, when artists wrestled with how to portray that which, by definition, cannot be portrayed. Midnight Service Dir. Kaylee Smith. 2025, 07 mins. U.S. On an evening exploring the liminal spaces of small-town Heber City, Utah, a girl lurks in the shadows, confronting her estranged contention with the religious culture. Sunset Smudge Dir. Jesse LoCascio. 2025, 8 mins. U.S., Amidst a sweltering heat wave, a young woman grapples with the slow decay and inevitable demise of her once beautiful surroundings. Let us see you again – تاني نش و ف ك خلينا Dir Lobna Morsi and Herlinde Raeman. 2026, 18 mins. Belgium. Let Us See You Again explores homecoming not as a destination, but as a journey between memory and present reality, belonging and transition. It is a tender, intergenerational epic about resilience, negotiation, and the continuous act of becoming. What do you see and hear in the quiet margins of a space when home is shaped by distance or time? How do you make room for a retour that is not merely a welcome, but also a farewell? Beneath the Concrete, the Forest Dir. Lev Omelchenko. 2026, 12 mins U.S. A short experimental documentary that takes us inside an ongoing struggle in the city of Atlanta, GA, between two sides to determine the future of Weelaunee, the biggest contiguous urban forest in the country. Atrium, or The Girl Who Painted Hats and Met the Sky Dir. Zoe Napurano. 2026, 06 mins. U.S. A young hat painter dreams of a strange lady. Why Look at Animals Dir. Maya Perry. 2019, 8 mins. U.S. Lo Sguardo (The Gaze) Dir. Gloria Zingales. 2024, 10 mins. U.S. When the news of an encroaching fire and an unsettling onlooker interrupt a night amongst friends, Sole—a young Italian woman—must return home alone. On her journey, Sole faces dangers that blur the line between reality and her own paranoia. Lo Sguardo is a short giallo thriller about the male gaze and its psychological effects on women. screenings.title: Our Body
screenings.description: Dir. Claire Simon. 2023, 168 mins. France. DCP. Master documentary filmmaker Simon (The Grocer’s Son, the Mayor, the Village and the World and Young Solitude) trains her camera on a gynecological ward in a public hospital in Paris. Over the course of many months of filming, and through interactions with a multitude of women, Simon captures a spectrum of fears, desires, and struggles, and a representation of women at all stages of life. In the process she questions what it means to live in a woman’s body, as well as how doctors, nurses, and medical institutions at large respond to myriad yet universal needs of patients—a group that, before this uncommonly generous and inclusive film reaches its conclusion, comes to include the filmmaker herself. screenings.title: The Rice Dumpling Vendors
screenings.description: With a wife, a mistress, three children, and a business that provides amply for all, Tsi-bing wants for nothing—that is, until his lover convinces him of his wife’s infidelity, breaks up their household, then clears off with all his cash, sending him tumbling down the socioeconomic ladder, taking odd jobs (including that of the film’s title) and striving to win back the spouse he’d foolishly spurned. One of nearly a thousand Taiyu Pian—films in which the characters speak in Taiwanese Minnan or Hokkien—produced in Taiwan between 1955 and 1981, and one of the crowning achievements of Taipei-born Hsin’s hugely prolific career.

screenings.title: Hercules in the Haunted World
screenings.description: Brit bodybuilder Reg Park straps on the sandals and exomis to play Zeus’s swole love child in Bava’s deliciously delirious peplum, co-written by Mondo Cane’s Franco Prosperi, which follows our hulking hero—as well as Theseus and Telemachus—on a perilous mission to save Herc’s lover Princess Deianira, stricken senseless by illness, endeavoring to procure for her a sacred stone from the depths of Hades, home court of Christopher Lee’s sinister Lyco and his zombie hordes. A triumph of resourcefulness over limited resources, rich with Gothic atmosphere, swirling with nigh-psychedelic colors, and offering at every turn ample evidence of cinematographer-turned-director Bava’s consummate mastery of the motion picture apparatus.

Irons gives one of the most complex and moving double performances in cinema history, playing twin gynecologists who develop a truly twisted relationship with a patient. While the brothers’ bizarre surgical instruments convey a memorable dose of body horror, the true horrors of Dead Ringers are psychological in Cronenberg’s brooding and outrageous exploration of a true story. screenings.title: Zu: Warriors from the Magic Mountain
screenings.description: Blood Demons, psychedelic lighting, cutting-edge special effects courtesy imported Hollywood technicians, head-lopping flying swords, physics-defying wire stunts, two Sammo Hungs, and Lin a vision of frigid majesty as an imperious Ice Queen—Hark’s brazen, eye-popping Tang Dynasty-set action-fantasy bonanza has a little bit of everything, and was one of the first wuxia to make a splash on the other side of the Pacific, an admitted influence on John Carpenter’s Hong Kong action-indebted Big Trouble in Little China (1986). The baroquely intricate plot involves a mystic mission into the mountains of Western China in search of legendary twin swords, while Hark himself is on a mission to see how much gonzo action he can fit into a single movie—one that’s breezily accomplished.

screenings.title: Next of Kin
screenings.description: Childless and unmarried, wealthy shipping magnate Kai Skaug has keeled over at age 54. With great expectations, his extended family—elderly mother, brother and sister with attendant spouses and offspring, assorted cousins—gather for his funeral and the reading of his will… thence to discover that this motley group, many very nearly strangers to one another, have been condemned to close collaboration, only to receive their share of inheritance if they agree to jointly operate the business that the late tycoon built as equal partners. An ensemble cast battle royale in which old resentments resurface alongside deep-buried secrets and bouts of blood-on-the-balls bickering alternate with episodes of remorseful self-recrimination, premiered in the main competition at the 32nd Cannes Film Festival.

screenings.description: Arranged to marry a rich man, young Ada (Mame Bineta Sane) is crushed when her true love goes missing at sea during a migration attempt — until a miracle reunites them. Winner of the Grand Prix at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival, Mati Diop’s haunting feature directorial debut made history as the first film directed by a Black woman to compete for the Palme d’Or. In Wolof, French and English with English subtitles.

Don't Play with Fire
screenings.description: Tsui’s outraged and outrageous third feature is a raw, tormented howl of hopeless rebellion that follows a trio of endorphin-addicted, bomb-planting teen nihilists as they get themselves involved with Triad thugs, gun runners, and—most perilous of all—a young woman (Chen-chi Lin) with a penchant for torturing small animals. Shredded by Hong Kong censors who blanched at its bloody-mindedness and its employment of shocking images from the city’s 1967 riots, Don’t Play with Fire (aka Dangerous Encounters of the First Kind) can be seen in a new restoration supervised by the director himself. An open provocation to anarchic upheaval, the blistering heat of its anti-establishment rage undiminished through the years.

screenings.title: The Witch Hunt
screenings.description: Set in the mountains of rugged western Norway in the early years of the 17th century, The Witch Hunt reunites Breien with Games of Love and Loneliness star Lil Terselius, here playing Eli—a young woman who returns to her native village after the failure of her marriage to find the locals in the grips of a superstitious persecutorial mania, a certitude that witches dwell in their midst, and a determination, on the part of the local patriarchs, to bring their punitive powers to bear against women who don’t tow the line. A film of somber beauty, winner of a Special Mention for Historical Reconstruction and a Best Actress prize at the 1981 Venice Film Festival.

screenings.description: “GERTRUD is as towering a master work in the narrative sound cinema as Brakhage’s THE ART OF VISION is in the nonnarrative cinema. Every detail, every motion, every word in GERTRUD has its right place, its own voice, and contributes to the whole and is beautiful. […] Every generation states its own position on love. GERTRUD is Dreyer’s statement on love, and it is pure, radiant, and perfect, like a ring.” –Jonas Mekas, MOVIE JOURNALCLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Uncut Gems
screenings.description: Adam Sandler gives a career-best performance as Howard Ratner, a fast-talking jeweler in Manhattan’s Diamond District with a penchant for living on the edge and well beyond his means, in the Safdies’ hectic, often hilarious thriller, where a debt-saddled Howie makes a series of high-stakes parlay bets on Kevin Garnett’s performance in the 2012 NBA playoffs that could lead to the windfall of a lifetime—or the abrupt end of his gambling career. “It’s gritty, but in the ’80s sense of it—gritty, with a lot of light and contrast. I started being a cinematographer in the ’80s, so they went back to this period of time where we were after very strong, ink blacks, very long lenses, very contrast-y images, very harsh contours… It was completely unlike anything I’ve done. I would never have thought I would photograph one day a movie like this. But it ended up being my favorite work, probably.” —Darius Khondji

screenings.title: Peking Opera Blues
screenings.description: Set in the newly established, vulnerable Republican China of 1913, Peking Opera Blues is a fizzily exuberant, chaotically colorful espionage thriller/screwball romance/slapstick social satire/costume drama pageant that bends genres and genders at will, wending together the stories of three irrepressible female protagonists—played by Sally Yeh, Brigitte Lin, and Cherie Chung, respectively here as a would-be star of the all-male Peking Opera stage, a warlord’s headstrong daughter, and a courtesan who’s copped a case of stolen jewels. Frenetic, filled with whiplash-inducing tonal shifts, frightfully enjoyable and, in the opinion of Quentin Tarantino, “one of the greatest films ever made.”

screenings.title: Night of the Living Dead
screenings.description: Shot outside of Pittsburgh at a fraction of the cost of a Hollywood feature by a band of filmmakers determined to make their mark, George A. Romero’s Night of the Living Dead is one of the great stories of independent cinema: a midnight hit turned box-office smash that became one of the most influential films of all time. A deceptively simple tale of a group of strangers trapped in a farmhouse who find themselves fending off a horde of flesh-eating ghouls newly arisen from their graves, Romero’s claustrophobic vision of a late-sixties America (literally) tearing itself apart rewrote the rules of the horror genre, combined gruesome gore with acute social commentary, and quietly broke ground by casting a black actor (Duane Jones) in the lead role.

screenings.director: Maria Jose Cuevas, Benjamin H. Stavillo
screenings.description: Mexico’s most iconic concert comes to U.S. theaters on September 15th, celebrating Mexican Independence Day and commemorating the 10th anniversary of Juan Gabriel’s passing. Experience his legendary first performance at Mexico City’s “Palacio de Bellas Artes” in 1990–a landmark event that forever transformed Mexican music. More than three decades later, this historic concert returns in a special theatrical release with newly restored picture and sound, plus an exclusive new opening featuring never-before-seen rehearsal footage from Juan Gabriel’s personal archive that offers a unique glimpse into the making of this unforgettable night. Every song, every standing ovation, and every iconic moment has been revitalized, allowing longtime fans and new audiences to experience this extraordinary performance like never before. Celebrate the timeless legacy of Juan Gabriel on the big screen in this once-in-a-generation cinematic event.

Comic when dealing in the foibles of its excellent ensemble cast and the mores of the urban bourgeoise, yet also possessed throughout by an air of unmistakable melancholy and lingering regret at missed opportunities, this feeling made all the deeper when one considers the great films Yang might still have produced. A work of epic length that avoids even a hint of bombast, dedicated instead to working its way into the hidden, niche spaces of everyday people’s emotional lives, it’s a film as rich and as sad as life itself.

screenings.title: Climate Film Festival Opening Night: House of Fish
screenings.description: Followed by a discussion with director Santiago Burin des Roziers and reception House of Fish Dir. Santiago Burin des Roziers. 2026, 85 mins. In Italian with English subtitles. At the crossroads of art, activism, and the ocean lies the extraordinary story of Paolo Fanciulli, a humble Italian fisherman with a revolutionary vision. After witnessing decades of destruction caused by illegal bottom trawling, Paolo devised a bold solution: an underwater museum of monumental marble sculptures that protect the seabed by preventing trawling while standing as powerful symbols of hope and resistance. House of Fish follows his remarkable journey, blending intimate personal storytelling with a natural history perspective on the fragile Mediterranean ecosystem. Through breathtaking underwater cinematography, the film reveals the devastating impact of industrial fishing on endangered marine life and vital habitats, including Posidonia oceanica, a seagrass essential to biodiversity and carbon capture. More than a conservation documentary, House of Fish is a cinematic celebration of courage, creativity, and community, inspiring audiences to reconnect with the ocean and recognize that one person’s vision can help transform the future of our seas. East Coast premiere. Followed by a reception from 9:00-11:00 p.m. Tickets: $20 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order Tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission. About the Climate Film Festival: The Climate Film Festival (CFF) is both an annual film festival held in New York City during Climate Week NYC and a year-round nonprofit cultural organization. Founded in 2023, CFF harnesses the power of motion pictures to reshape the conversation around climate change, making urgent issues accessible, engaging, and action-oriented through the cinematic lens. Each year, the festival presents a curated selection of scripted, documentary, feature, short, episodic, and experimental works, alongside filmmaker conversations, educational programming, and the Narrative Change Summit. Committed to formal innovation, environmental justice, and community engagement, CFF amplifies bold voices and inspiring films that reframe the conversation around climate action. Special Guest: Santiago Burin des Roziers was born in Buenos Aires, Argentina and moved to London to pursue a career in filmmaking. Not long after film school, he started directing. His projects have taken him around the globe, to over 30 countries. He has made films for the BBC, Channel 4 and VICE, as well as for brands such as Coca– Cola, Sony, Red Bull, and Adidas.

screenings.description: “In 1964, an enterprising psychologist (Dr. Everett Shostrom) persuaded a 30-year-old waitress and single mother, to take part in filmed psychotherapy sessions, with three of the most influential psychologists of the 20th century. The resulting series, THREE APPROACHES TO PSYCHOTHERAPY (1965), was primary training material in the field for decades. screenings.description: The fourth and final film by Kon takes place in a not-too-distant future in which therapists, using a new technology called DC Mini, are able to record the dreams of psychiatric patients. All well and good, until a raid on the lab leads to the loss of the DC Mini prototype and a bleed between the troubled subconscious images and reality, leading to a race-against-time to stop bedlam from breaking out in the streets. An admitted inspiration for Christopher Nolan’s Inception (2010), though far more visually extravagant in its vibrant, psychedelia-inflected imaginings, which climax in a thrilling, terrifying dream apocalypse burst from Kon’s fervid imagination.

screenings.title: Oedipus Rex
screenings.description: Seeking source materials from which to forge a new “primal cinema,” Pasolini delved into the storehouse of mythic heritage. Taking on Sophocles’s Oedipus Rex, he begins with a prologue set in prewar Italy, and goes on to defy expectation throughout, depicting Oedipus (Franco Citti), unknowingly betrothed to biological mother Silvana Mangano, as a victim of his own ignorant innocence, here far from an unambiguously positive virtue. Pasolini’s first film in color, featuring costumes and art direction that evoke an almost science fiction vision of the ancient world, and a showy role for Carmelo Bene, then-reigning bad boy of Italian stage and screen.

screenings.title: Zu: Warriors from the Magic Mountain
screenings.description: Blood Demons, psychedelic lighting, cutting-edge special effects courtesy imported Hollywood technicians, head-lopping flying swords, physics-defying wire stunts, two Sammo Hungs, and Lin a vision of frigid majesty as an imperious Ice Queen—Hark’s brazen, eye-popping Tang Dynasty-set action-fantasy bonanza has a little bit of everything, and was one of the first wuxia to make a splash on the other side of the Pacific, an admitted influence on John Carpenter’s Hong Kong action-indebted Big Trouble in Little China (1986). The baroquely intricate plot involves a mystic mission into the mountains of Western China in search of legendary twin swords, while Hark himself is on a mission to see how much gonzo action he can fit into a single movie—one that’s breezily accomplished.

screenings.description: Pasolini’s thrillingly freeform, intellectually adventurous documentary, narrated in the style of thoughts dashed off in a notebook, charts his preparations to make a film of Aeschylus’s Oresteia trilogy in Tanzania, Ethiopia, and Uganda. Forming a trilogy of sorts with previous Greek tragedy adaptations Oedipus Rex and Medea—a trilogy that, in the phrasing of scholar Daniel Humphrey, encapsulates Pasolini’s paradoxical “archaic modernism”—Notes Toward an African Orestes proposes metaphorical parallels between the source texts and events following the emergence of many African nations into independence, and also finds the filmmaker testing his own presumptions and prejudices against the lived experience of African students at the University of Rome.

screenings.description: Screening followed by a Q&A with special guests. Dir. Penny Lane. 2026, 95 mins. U.S. DCP. Flaco, a Eurasian Eagle-Owl, escapes from the Central Park Zoo and sets off on a magical odyssey through the island of Manhattan. An apex predator with 2-inch talons, a 6-foot wingspan and piercing pumpkin-orange eyes, Flaco overcomes his years of captivity and lack of survival skills to answer the call of the wild—and discovers he was wild inside all along. This one-of-a-kind owl’s epic song is sung in Wild Inside by a chorus of besotted New Yorkers—young and old, bird-nerds and civilians, many of them immigrants themselves—all of them reaching for a glimpse of the wild, a glimmer of magic, or even just someone to believe in. The remarkable story of Flaco raises some questions: is it right to keep a bird in a cage? How can we be better to our nonhuman neighbors? Courtesy Sandbox Films. Watch the trailer here. A handsomely mounted and deeply felt period melodrama spanning the years between 1897 and 1912, redolent with regret concerning opportunities not seized and roads not taken.

screenings.title: ACE Presents: Pumping Iron
screenings.description: The movie that set Arnold Schwarzenegger off on his way to becoming a household name (admittedly one that Americans had difficulty pronouncing) and that introduced gym rat subculture to the wider world, Butler and Fiore’s paean to pecs follows golden boy Arnie on a collision course with Brooklyn-bred big man Lou Ferrigno, going bicep-to-bicep with the future Incredible Hulk at the 1975 Mr. Universe and Mr. Olympia competitions. Nimbly constructed by editors Geof Bartz, ACE and the late Larry Silk, ACE, and finally released in theaters after two years and many a financial worry on the part of its producers, Pumping Iron is a documentary that plays like a finely tuned sports drama, with Ferrigno as affable, down-to-earth underdog and Schwarzenegger as the beaming, boisterous heavy that you can’t help but like.

screenings.title: The Gloria of Your Imagination
screenings.description: “In 1964, an enterprising psychologist (Dr. Everett Shostrom) persuaded a 30-year-old waitress and single mother, to take part in filmed psychotherapy sessions, with three of the most influential psychologists of the 20th century. The resulting series, THREE APPROACHES TO PSYCHOTHERAPY (1965), was primary training material in the field for decades. With the immersive double projection of THE GLORIA OF YOUR IMAGINATION, Reeves creates an intricate, superimposed montage of Gloria’s unguarded sessions with numerous film artifacts of her lifetime: newsreels, home movies, commercials, a beauty pageant, Cold War propaganda, and educational films. The result sees viewers absorbing the culture of that era directly through Reeves’s mix of intimate storytelling and sense of curiosity.” –WEXNER CENTER FOR THE ARTSThe screening on Fri, Sept 18 will involve 16mm + digital dual projection; the screenings on Sat & Sun, Sept 19 & 20 will be of the single-channel DCP version of the film.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Next of Kin
screenings.description: Childless and unmarried, wealthy shipping magnate Kai Skaug has keeled over at age 54. With great expectations, his extended family—elderly mother, brother and sister with attendant spouses and offspring, assorted cousins—gather for his funeral and the reading of his will… thence to discover that this motley group, many very nearly strangers to one another, have been condemned to close collaboration, only to receive their share of inheritance if they agree to jointly operate the business that the late tycoon built as equal partners. An ensemble cast battle royale in which old resentments resurface alongside deep-buried secrets and bouts of blood-on-the-balls bickering alternate with episodes of remorseful self-recrimination, premiered in the main competition at the 32nd Cannes Film Festival.

Working in his native Italy for the first time in 15 years, and in his only collaboration with DP Darius Khondji, Bertolucci creates a film of warm, mellow light; lyrical grace notes; and exquisite performances from Tyler, Joseph Fiennes, Jeremy Irons, Rachel Weisz, and others.

screenings.title: When It Was Blue
screenings.description: WHEN IT WAS BLUE rejoices in the splendor of nature as the camera eye traverses land and sea in a montage of diverse ecosystems from the Americas to Iceland and New Zealand. Reeves creates colorful, organic textures and forms, inspired by elements of the natural world, using an array of direct-on-film techniques. This abstract imagery is superimposed upon wildlife footage, generating depth while merging the powerful intricacies of nature with an artist’s reverence for it. With her Bolex, Reeves hurries to “capture” the natural world before it vanishes. Join Tim Curry, Barry Bostwick, Susan Sarandon and rock star Meatloaf in the most popular cult classic of all time.​

screenings.title: Don't Play with Fire
screenings.description: Tsui’s outraged and outrageous third feature is a raw, tormented howl of hopeless rebellion that follows a trio of endorphin-addicted, bomb-planting teen nihilists as they get themselves involved with Triad thugs, gun runners, and—most perilous of all—a young woman (Chen-chi Lin) with a penchant for torturing small animals. Shredded by Hong Kong censors who blanched at its bloody-mindedness and its employment of shocking images from the city’s 1967 riots, Don’t Play with Fire (aka Dangerous Encounters of the First Kind) can be seen in a new restoration supervised by the director himself. An open provocation to anarchic upheaval, the blistering heat of its anti-establishment rage undiminished through the years.

The Birds
screenings.description: Dir. Alfred Hitchcock. 1963, 119 mins. U.S. 4K DCP. With Tippi Hedren, Rod Taylor, Jessica Tandy, Veronica Cartwright. Tippi Hedren’s cursed Melanie Daniels (swathed in an iconic pale green coat and skirt ensemble from Edith Head) is the glamorous centerpiece to Hitchcock’s existential horror classic, her brilliantly placid performance as eerily frightening as the squawking gulls that engulf her one horrible weekend in Bodega Bay. screenings.title: Yi Yi
screenings.description: The last work of a master filmmaker who died far too young, the gentle, restrained, and terribly humane Yi Yi observes the interplay between three generations of an upper middle-class Taipei family. Comic when dealing in the foibles of its excellent ensemble cast and the mores of the urban bourgeoise, yet also possessed throughout by an air of unmistakable melancholy and lingering regret at missed opportunities, this feeling made all the deeper when one considers the great films Yang might still have produced. A work of epic length that avoids even a hint of bombast, dedicated instead to working its way into the hidden, niche spaces of everyday people’s emotional lives, it’s a film as rich and as sad as life itself.

screenings.title: Paint Me a Road Out of Here + Q&A | Presented by Miss Video 4 U
screenings.description: In 1971, artist Faith Ringgold created a monumental painting “For the Women’s House” for the women incarcerated at Rikers Island jail. Fifty years later, artist Mary Enoch Elizabeth Baxter, who gave birth in prison 15 years ago, finds herself banding together with an eclectic group of activists, politicians, artists, corrections officers and Faith Ringgold herself to free the artwork with the ultimate goal of freeing the women. Paint Me a Road Out of Here is a wild tale of the painting’s whitewashed journey and the two artists who challenged the same powerful and oppressive institutions, a half century apart, with their artwork, their voices and their shared, persistent goals.

screenings.title: Nct 127 5th Tour 'neo City : Seoul - the Redline' in Cinemas
screenings.director: Kyungchan Kim, Doyeon Kim, Soyoung Park
screenings.language: English and Korean with English subtitles
screenings.description: NCT 127 5TH TOUR ‘NEO CITY : SEOUL - THE REDLINE’ in CINEMAS brings the explosive opening of NCT 127’s long -awaited return to the big screen through a special live viewing event in theaters around the world. Marking the group’s first tour in a year and eight months, this event captures the scale, energy, and electr ifying performances of NCT 127 as they kick off a new chapter of NEO CITY in Seoul. Broadcast live from KSPO DOME, audiences worldwide are invited to experience the intensity of the concert in a cinematic setting, taking in every moment of the setlist, staging, and onstage charisma with fans across the globe. For NCTzens and K -pop audienc es alike, this cinematic experience is a chance to witness the heat of THE REDLINE together, beyond borders, on the biggest screen possible!

screenings.title: Wives III
screenings.description: A surprise 50th birthday party for Kaja (Katja Medbøe) thrown on a city streetcar by old school chums Heidrun and Mie (Frøydis Armand and Anne Marie Ottersen) turns into another conversational bender in the third entry of Breien’s very singular franchise, in which the pleasure the central trio take in one another’s company is very much contagious. Deferred dreams, children reaching the cusp of adulthood, aging parents on the verge of the hereafter, husbands and lovers—it’s all grist for the mill in this wry, wistful, and very moving capstone to the trilogy, with Oslo’s Independence Day providing a jubilant background to their final round of playing hooky.

screenings.title: The Gloria of Your Imagination
screenings.description: “In 1964, an enterprising psychologist (Dr. Everett Shostrom) persuaded a 30-year-old waitress and single mother, to take part in filmed psychotherapy sessions, with three of the most influential psychologists of the 20th century. The resulting series, THREE APPROACHES TO PSYCHOTHERAPY (1965), was primary training material in the field for decades. With the immersive double projection of THE GLORIA OF YOUR IMAGINATION, Reeves creates an intricate, superimposed montage of Gloria’s unguarded sessions with numerous film artifacts of her lifetime: newsreels, home movies, commercials, a beauty pageant, Cold War propaganda, and educational films. The result sees viewers absorbing the culture of that era directly through Reeves’s mix of intimate storytelling and sense of curiosity.” –WEXNER CENTER FOR THE ARTSThe screening on Fri, Sept 18 will involve 16mm + digital dual projection; the screenings on Sat & Sun, Sept 19 & 20 will be of the single-channel DCP version of the film.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Stray Dogs
screenings.description: Tsai’s devastating minimalist portrait of urban desolation, destitution and defeat is a gorgeous cinematic lament starring Lee Kang-sheng as a single father of two who ekes out a subsistence living by working as a human signboard while his hungry children wile their days away in the supermarket, where they’ll encounter a protector in the person of manager Chen Shiang-chyi.

screenings.title: Se7en
screenings.description: Nearing-retirement veteran Detective Morgan Freeman and new transfer Brad Pitt track a serial killer with an advanced sense of stagecraft through a sickly, perpetually sodden city of peeling lead paint and lost souls in Fincher’s tour de force, easily one of the most stylistically influential films of the 1990s. “The look of Se7en … came out of this tight working ‘cell’ we created between David, myself, the production designer Arthur Max, and the costume designer Michael Kaplan. The four of us would meet together to discuss the art direction and visual scope of the movie, and we did several sessions like that to establish a unified plan… There was something [about Robert Frank’s photos in The Americans] that interested me, which was related to the grittiness of them, the blandness, the loneliness of a past era and the texture of death.” —Darius Khondji

screenings.title: Wings of Desire + Hidden in Pieces
screenings.description: Wings of Desire is one of cinema’s loveliest city symphonies. Bruno Ganz is Damiel, an angel perched atop buildings high over Berlin who can hear the thoughts—fears, hopes, dreams—of all the people living below. But when he falls in love with a beautiful trapeze artist, he is willing to give up his immortality and come back to earth to be with her. Made not long before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this stunning tapestry of sounds and images, shot in black and white and color by the legendary Henri Alekan, forever made the name of director Wim Wenders synonymous with film art.

screenings.title: Narrow Rooms: Jerker
screenings.description: In a San Francisco apartment, in 1985, Bert is just about to fall asleep when a stranger named J.R. calls. “You hard?” he asks Bert, and the two begin a hot and heavy phone sex session that soon turns into a nightly routine. Over the span of a year, we watch as Bert (Tom Wagner) and J.R. (Joseph Stachura) explore their fantasies, get each other off, and forge a deeper connection that allows them to open up to each other about their fears and sorrows surrounding the AIDS epidemic, all without ever meeting face to face. Playwright Robert Chesley wryly called his groundbreaking 1986 play JERKER “a pornographic elegy with redeeming social value and a hymn to the queer men of San Francisco,” which perhaps sought to preempt the inevitable criticism and censorship of the play’s unabashedly sex-positive dialogue. Hugh Harrison’s smart, rarely seen 1991 adaptation combines the rich, raunchy text of Chesley’s play with the shot-on-video aesthetics of late 1980s gay adult films, making us feel as if we’re watching an especially well-written Jeff Stryker or Joey Stefano movie. Help us celebrate the 40th anniversary of JERKER’s theatrical premiere with this very special screening.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Fat Girl
screenings.description: Twelve-year-old Anaïs is fat. Her sister, fifteen-year-old Elena, is a beauty. While the girls are on vacation with their parents, Anaïs tags along as Elena explores the dreary seaside town. Elena meets Fernando, an Italian law student; he seduces her with promises of love, and the ever watchful Anaïs bears witness to the corruption of her sister’s innocence. FAT GIRL is not only a portrayal of female adolescent sexuality and the complicated bond between siblings but also a shocking assertion by the always controversial Catherine Breillat that violent oppression exists at the core of male-female relations.

screenings.title: Screamplay
screenings.description: Edgar Allan (Rufus B. Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies…only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (played by underground film legend George Kuchar). When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad.SCREAMPLAY is a marvel of campy charm, gothic horror tropes, and astonishingly inventive set design and special effects. Wearing its low-budget resourcefulness on its sleeve, but also genuinely atmospheric and transporting, the spell it casts is all the more remarkable given that it was filmed almost entirely within the confines of the 3,200-square-foot South End Boston loft where director Rufus Butler Seder and his Boston Black and White Movie Company (comprised of fellow students from the city’s School of the Museum of Fine Arts) had previously made a bevy of similarly inspired 16mm short films. Conjured from some of the earliest and still-most-effective cinematic techniques – matte paintings, scale models, ingeniously adaptable sets, animation, highly expressionistic lighting, and the good old-fashioned magic provided by charismatic performers (above all, Seder himself in the central role, and of course the irreplaceable George Kuchar, who broke his ankle during filming of the final fight scene) – SCREAMPLAY is a deliriously entertaining demonstration of the power of low budget invention, and a singularly charming (Boston) salute to Old Hollywood.Premiered (alongside BLOOD SIMPLE) at the 1985 New York Independent Film Festival, initially distributed by Troma (click here for details about our upcoming Troma series), but rarely screened in recent decades, SCREAMPLAY has been newly restored in 4K – scanned from Seder’s personal 16mm print – and is now back in circulation, where it’s poised to charm, delight, and frighten a whole new audience.Preceded by:Rufus Butler SederIN THE CITY: A TRILOGY (LIVE IN FEAR; SUN RUN; PHANTOM SUBWAYS)1977, 6 min, 16mm-to-DCPWriter, director, and star Rufus Butler Seder and producer and cinematographer Dennis M. screenings.title: 60 Years of Jim Henson’s Time Piece
screenings.description: In 1965, Jim Henson made Time Piece, an experimental nine-minute short film that tells what he called “the story of Everyman, frustrated by the typical tasks of a typical day.” The film opens with a man—played by Henson—in a hospital bed. A doctor takes his pulse. The pulse turns into a drumbeat, which becomes the percussive soundtrack for the film, in a syncopated score created by Don Sebesky. Through a series of jump cuts, we follow the man as he walks through city streets, then suburban streets, and then the jungle. Playfully surreal sequences are bridged by short passages of stop-motion animation. As Henson described his filmmaking goals: “In Time Piece I was playing with a kind of flow of consciousness form of editing, where the image took you to another image, and there was no logic to it but your mind put it together.” While the film retains his trademark sense of humor, it is also a bold example of nonlinear editing. Time Piece played for a year at the Paris Theatre in Manhattan, along with the French art-house hit A Man and a Woman. Henson’s film was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Short Film. It remains fresh today as both a time capsule of 1960s experimental filmmaking, and as a brilliantly conceived and edited example of Henson’s creativity. Karen Falk, Archives Director of The Jim Henson Company and Vice President of The Jim Henson Legacy, will follow the screening with an in-depth look of how the film was produced, sharing materials from Jim Henson’s original production files and photography. The film is presented courtesy of The Jim Henson Company. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Screamplay
screenings.description: Edgar Allan (Rufus B. Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies…only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (played by underground film legend George Kuchar). When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad.SCREAMPLAY is a marvel of campy charm, gothic horror tropes, and astonishingly inventive set design and special effects. Wearing its low-budget resourcefulness on its sleeve, but also genuinely atmospheric and transporting, the spell it casts is all the more remarkable given that it was filmed almost entirely within the confines of the 3,200-square-foot South End Boston loft where director Rufus Butler Seder and his Boston Black and White Movie Company (comprised of fellow students from the city’s School of the Museum of Fine Arts) had previously made a bevy of similarly inspired 16mm short films. Conjured from some of the earliest and still-most-effective cinematic techniques – matte paintings, scale models, ingeniously adaptable sets, animation, highly expressionistic lighting, and the good old-fashioned magic provided by charismatic performers (above all, Seder himself in the central role, and of course the irreplaceable George Kuchar, who broke his ankle during filming of the final fight scene) – SCREAMPLAY is a deliriously entertaining demonstration of the power of low budget invention, and a singularly charming (Boston) salute to Old Hollywood.Premiered (alongside BLOOD SIMPLE) at the 1985 New York Independent Film Festival, initially distributed by Troma (click here for details about our upcoming Troma series), but rarely screened in recent decades, SCREAMPLAY has been newly restored in 4K – scanned from Seder’s personal 16mm print – and is now back in circulation, where it’s poised to charm, delight, and frighten a whole new audience.Preceded by:Rufus Butler SederIN THE CITY: A TRILOGY (LIVE IN FEAR; SUN RUN; PHANTOM SUBWAYS)1977, 6 min, 16mm-to-DCPWriter, director, and star Rufus Butler Seder and producer and cinematographer Dennis M. screenings.title: Fat Girl
screenings.description: Twelve-year-old Anaïs is fat. Her sister, fifteen-year-old Elena, is a beauty. While the girls are on vacation with their parents, Anaïs tags along as Elena explores the dreary seaside town. Elena meets Fernando, an Italian law student; he seduces her with promises of love, and the ever watchful Anaïs bears witness to the corruption of her sister’s innocence. FAT GIRL is not only a portrayal of female adolescent sexuality and the complicated bond between siblings but also a shocking assertion by the always controversial Catherine Breillat that violent oppression exists at the core of male-female relations.

screenings.description: In Still Film, his imaginative, incisive ode to movie culture and its beguiling hold on our imagination, Brooklyn-based artist-filmmaker James N. Kienitz Wilkins takes four decades of moving-image circulation to task. The film’s narration, modeled on an actual legal deposition, accompanies a procession of 35mm publicity stills culled by Wilkins from studio press kits. As the film runs through its carousel of Hollywood imagery of yesteryear, the courtroom characters—all performed by Wilkins himself, in his characteristically gravelly, rapid-fire voice—address the shapeshifting nature and mythologizing power of the moviegoing experience. Swirling around unverified facts and conspiracy theories while touching on the technological obsolescence and arcane obsessions that fuel true cinephila today, Wilkins’s playful, subjective journey interrogates the subject of truth itself.

screenings.title: Common Carrier | Four by James N. Kienitz Wilkins
screenings.description: A collection of vignettes and conversations with various full-time and part-time artists, several featuring Wilkins himself, the kaleidoscopic Common Carrier’s images are almost entirely “overlapped,” as are its dialogues, which among other things address schizophrenia, mystical “aura,” division of labor, and constitutional law, these varied discussions sharing the soundtrack with disparate radio feeds from WNYC and Hot 97 that are united by the recurrence of the word “work.” A rich and ruminative film about making do in the 21st century, eking out a creative existence in the scant free time that’s left over after the other obligations have been met.
